absent: Definitions and numeric values of mitigation mode enums and their string tables for Spectre, Retbleed, MDS, TAA, MMIO, RFDS, SRBDS, SRSO, GDS, ITS, TSA and VMSCAPE.
Numeric MSR identifiers and bit definitions for test control split lock and debug control bus lock fields.
Layout of pt_regs, thread fault fields, device show callback registration, and per-CPU TLB state beyond the cached CR4 use shown.
Implementation and initialization of bus lock semaphore, unlock delayed work item, rate limit helpers and sysctl registration helpers.
Feature and bug flag values and semantics for split lock, bus lock, VMX, SMT, hypervisor and all X86 bug entries.
Scheduling, sleep, CPU pinning and signal delivery contracts for warn, throttle and fatal paths.
Full update and apply function bodies for each mitigation beyond ordering and dependency notes shown.
Vendor, model and microcode checks, eBPF policy query, static key mechanics and command line parsing helpers.

findings.text: Mitigation selection runs as an ordered update phase followed by an ordered apply phase, with documented dependencies where later selectors observe earlier results for Spectre V2, Retbleed, Indirect Target Selection, user STIBP handling and SRSO before all per-issue apply steps execute.

L1 Terminal Fault reporting centers on a default PTE inversion concept plus a VMX mode table with six enumerated flush behaviors covering automatic choice, never, conditional, always, EPT disabled and not required, each associated with a distinct human readable label.

Full L1TF status reporting varies with configuration: automatic mode yields a short form, EPT-disabled and never-with-SMT cases yield a two-part form, and other modes yield a three-part form including SMT posture; a reduced build always yields only the short default form.

Instruction TLB multihit reporting distinguishes unsupported virtualization, disabled virtualization observed through the cached CR4 shadow, mitigated split-huge-page operation, and vulnerable operation; a reduced build reports only a generic vulnerable indication.
Cached CR4 reader exposes the current CPU copy of control register state held in per-CPU TLB state for use by feature and virtualization checks.

Microarchitectural Data Sampling, TSX asynchronous abort and MMIO stale data reporters share a pattern where hypervisor execution adds an unknown host qualifier and bare metal adds an SMT qualifier, with special handling for off states and for MSBDS-only parts.

Register File Data Sampling, Indirect Target Selection, Special Register Buffer Data Sampling, Speculative Return Stack Overflow, Gather Data Sampling, Transient Scheduler Attacks and VMSCAPE each report a single per-mode string, while old microcode reports unknown under hypervisor and vulnerable otherwise.

Spectre V2 status combines a base mode string with optional qualifiers for indirect branch prediction barrier behavior, firmware IBRS, STIBP posture, return stack buffer filling, PBRSB protection, Branch History Injection posture and module taint, with early vulnerable overrides involving unprivileged extended BPF with enhanced IBRS variants and SMT.

STIBP suffix reflects user mode selection and conditional switch state with an empty result in enhanced IBRS without automatic IBRS; IBPB suffix reflects feature presence and always versus conditional switch keys; PBRSB suffix reflects bug presence and VM-exit return stack protections; BHI suffix prioritizes not-affected, hardware, software loop, retpoline and VM-exit cases.

Retbleed reporting treats untrained return and IBPB modes specially by rejecting non-AMD style vendors as vulnerable and otherwise qualifying SMT posture with disabled, STIBP-protected or vulnerable outcomes; all other modes report a single per-mode string.

Common vulnerability show dispatcher first reports not affected when the queried bug flag is clear, then delegates each known bug to its dedicated reporter with Meltdown checking page table isolation and Xen paravirtual context and L1TF gated on PTE inversion support, falling back to a generic vulnerable indication.

Per-vulnerability sysfs show routines for Meltdown, Spectre variants, store bypass, L1TF, MDS, TSX abort, ITLB multihit, SRBDS, MMIO, Retbleed, SRSO, GDS, RFDS, old microcode, Indirect Target Selection, TSA and VMSCAPE are exported as thin wrappers around the common dispatcher.
Unpatched return thunk notifier raises a one-time warning indicating unexpected use of an unpatched return sequence.

Interrupted safe-return fixup runs without instrumentation and emulates completion of a return sequence by adjusting stack and instruction pointers, with extra stack compensation when interrupted at either of two safe return trampolines before loading the return address from the stack.
Safe-return fixup dereferences the task stack pointer to fetch a return address, so callers must guarantee a valid readable stack and correct register context because no validation is shown.
Split lock detection uses four ordered states representing disabled, warning, fatal and rate-limited operation, with disabled as the zero value and the remaining states in increasing order.

Boot option table pairs textual names with detection states including a prefix form for rate limiting; sysctl table exposes an unsigned integer mitigation toggle under kernel with zero to one bounds; rate limit state and per-CPU delayed work objects hold throttle and re-arm state.

Detection state defaults to warning only when split or bus lock features are present, otherwise remains disabled, and an optional boot command line token can override it by exact name match except for the rate limit form which also carries a numeric argument.

Rate limit option accepts only positive bus lock rates up to one thousand per second, initializing a per-second throttle that reports on release; other spellings require exact full-length equality with the known option names.

Split lock control is probed by toggling its test control bit with safe accesses and comparing readback, caching the firmware value at init, forcing the feature flag on success, and thereafter updating the control register from the cached value with the enable bit added or omitted.

Per-CPU split lock initialization disables alignment checking in rate limit mode and otherwise programs the test control bit from global state when the model allows; bus lock initialization programs the debug control bus lock bit unless warning or fatal split handling or disabled state routes through alignment faults; delayed work and sysctl registration occur at init.

Split and bus lock traps form a mode-driven machine where warning paths log rate-limited diagnostics and attempt forward progress, rate limit mode throttles bus locks before warning, fatal mode terminates with bus error, disabled mode ignores bus locks, and offlined CPUs re-enable detection.

Split lock warning path serializes mitigated execution with an interruptible bus lock semaphore held across a short delayed re-enable, using a shared unlock work item when mitigation is enabled and a per-CPU re-enable work item otherwise, with CPU pinning around work selection.

Fault-time mitigation may sleep interruptibly for short fixed delays and may block on semaphore acquisition, aborting mitigation without progress if interrupted; MSR probe failure permanently leaves detection disabled with an informational message.

Guest and fatal split or bus lock handling reports alignment faults using bus error with alignment code and records an alignment-check trap number with cleared error code in thread fault state; user split handling refuses mitigation when the alignment flag is already set or fatal mode is active.

Public bus and split lock operations comprise per-CPU init, guest trap filter returning whether the guest was warned, user trap filter returning whether mitigation was applied, and bus lock trap handler plus offline re-enable hook.
Bus lock component tags its log output with an x86 split lock detection prefix.
